title: Is whitespace around type="module" stripped?
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

When looking at the script element in SVG for the SVG 2 spec, I found this issue. It's not totally clear. 

The current text of [prepare the script element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#prepare-the-script-element), step 8, says:

> Otherwise, if el has a [type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-script-type) attribute, then let the script block's type string be the value of that attribute with [leading and trailing ASCII whitespace stripped](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-leading-and-trailing-ascii-whitespace).

So `<script type=" module ">` is a module script. 

Working only in Firefox. 
Not Working in Safari and Chrome.

## History

* #7018 (2021): Safari, Firefox and Chrome all rejected `type=" module "`. Commit 23c723e3e94103e495a6b67e60ffc8a1a164334b ("Do not strip whitespaces for non-classic script type attribute") moved the stripping into the JavaScript MIME type check only, so `module` had to match exactly.
* #7923 (2022): `language="javascript "` should not have its whitespace stripped. Commit 36470c17827635ee0604554e3df33de71e69dc11 ("Do not whitespace-strip `<script>`'s language="" attribute") moved the stripping back onto the type attribute value, which applies it to `module`, `importmap` and `speculationrules` again.

#7923 does not mention module scripts, so undoing #7018 looks like a side effect.

## Practical test

```html
<script type=" module ">
  // runs as a module per the current text
</script>
```

| Browser | `type=" module "` | `type=" text/javascript "` |
| -------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| Safari Technology Preview 253 | not run | runs |
| Firefox 159 | runs as a module | runs |
| Chrome 157 | not run | runs |

And the code references in browsers:

* WebKit strips whitespace only for the JavaScript MIME type check, then compares `module` with the raw value: [ScriptElement.cpp](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/d0902945e7f10b0de81446ff13a51ea3c9056ca6/Source/WebCore/dom/ScriptElement.cpp#L182-L195)
* Chromium does the same: [script_loader.cc](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/6513e990f866627755d0fe4e6a5195b2dfdc6134/third_party/blink/renderer/core/script/script_loader.cc#L453-L466)
* Gecko strips the whole value first, for HTML and SVG `script`: [ScriptElement.cpp](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/8c938d56856ad3cc9965dff55c0fc47c0d493a57/dom/script/ScriptElement.cpp#L322-L345)

By the code, `importmap` and `speculationrules` with whitespace split the same way. 
I only tested `module`.

## WPT wrong?

[module/type.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/52110495e3b415aad0b3b95f60273ddea24d4cb6/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-script-element/module/type.html) still expects the 2021 behaviour, but its two whitespace cases cannot fail:

```html
<script type="module ">window.t4.unreached_func('Unexpectedly evaluated');</script>
<script type=" module">window.t5.unreached_func('Unexpectedly evaluated');</script>
```

`unreached_func()` returns a function and nothing calls it, so the test passes even in Firefox, whose code strips the whitespace and runs both scripts.


Which behaviour is intended?

1. The 2021 one: strip whitespace only for the JavaScript MIME type check, while keeping #7923's fix for `language`. This matches Safari and Chrome, and Firefox would change.
2. The current text. Safari and Chrome would change.

Either way, WPT module/type.html needs the missing `()` so that it can fail.
